title: Bounded construction of a doubling table
statement: Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a set of machine limits, $P$ a program, $d$ a call depth, $\mu$ a memory function, and $x$ an integer. Let $M,V,fr,a$ be natural numbers such that $a\le V$, $1\le M$, the space limit is at most the word limit, $4V+4M+16$ is at most the word limit, and $fr+\bigl(\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\bigr)$ is at most the space limit. Set $r$ equal to the number of binary digits of $\lfloor a/M\rfloor$. Starting with locals $[x,M,fr,a,0,M]$ and memory $\mu$, the table-building program has an execution of cost at most $19r+6$ whose final locals are $[x,M,fr,a,r,M2^r]$, and whose final memory $\mu'$ satisfies $\mu'(fr+j)=M2^j$ for every $j<r$ and agrees with $\mu$ at every address below $fr$.
